songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World

ai_show_review.summary: Ferocious Dark Star marathon with twin Lovelights and tight St. Stephen>Eleven
ai_show_review.blurb: The set roars with a blistering Dark Star that segues into Me & My Uncle, followed by a rare twin‑Lovelight sandwich framing Saint Stephen > The Eleven. Jerry’s guitar soars while Mickey’s drums add the quirky bird‑chirp texture, and the encore delivers a heartfelt Morning Dew.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds on April 27 at Labor Temple is a single‑set blaze that captures the Dead at a peak of exploratory intensity. The evening launches with a Turn On Your Lovelight that immediately dives into Me & My Uncle, setting up an indifferent but serviceable Sitting On Top Of The World before launching into a Dark Star that stretches and morphs, pulling Jerry’s lead lines into a soaring dialogue with Phil’s bass. After the Star‑burst, the band rolls straight into Saint Stephen > The Eleven, then returns for a second Turn On Your Lovelight, creating a memorable “Lovelight sandwich” that frames one of the tightest eleven‑minute explorations of the era. Throughout, Mickey Hart’s drumming is crystal clear on the excellent soundboard source, even contributing an unmistakable bird‑chirp percussive accent that adds a mystical flavor. The night closes with a plaintive Morning Dew, giving the marathon a gentle, reflective coda after the high‑octane journey.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with crisp, well‑balanced mix and no dropouts, preserving the band’s dynamics and the signature bird‑chirp percussion.

key_highlights: Explosive Dark Star that expands into Me & My Uncle
Twin Turn On Your Lovelight sandwich framing Saint Stephen > The Eleven
Mickey Hart’s distinctive bird‑chirp percussion adds mystic texture
Exceptional soundboard clarity captures every nuance of the performance

band_performance.Jerry: His guitar work shines – soaring leads in Dark Star, crisp tones throughout the Lovelight sandwich, and a playful lick during Me & My Uncle.
band_performance.Phil: Strong interaction with Jerry on Dark Star, providing powerful bass foundation; occasional looseness in Me & My Uncle but overall solid presence.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are clearly audible; his playing drives the high energy and adds the quirky bird‑chirp percussion that colors the performance.
